key_insight: Routine clinical data available at the first echocardiogram can help shortlist the most likely genetic conditions in infants with congenital heart disease.
clinical_relevance: This could support earlier genetic suspicion and triage in CHD care, especially before definitive genetic testing results are available.
method: Retrospective single-center cohort of 1,720 children with congenital heart disease and known genetic testing status.
Compared class-balanced logistic regression with a multimodal deep learning fusion model as more data became available over time.
Evaluated balanced top-3 accuracy after echocardiogram data, then after serial records, radiology notes, and ICD-10 codes were added.
evidence_signal: Balanced top-3 accuracy was 0.758 using echocardiogram-visit data alone and increased to 0.809 with later clinical codes; multimodal fusion performed similarly.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data and moderate class imbalance may limit generalizability, and the model should be validated prospectively before clinical use.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Modeling to Aid in the Identification of Genetic Conditions in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease
